selection.reason: Best fit for a real early-access website product: makes the mechanism and useful outcome immediately visible while maintaining a direct invitation.

prompt_expansion.reframing: The homepage must make a real business website product immediately understandable and worth trying. Put the product's useful interaction at the center, and let visual craft make that explanation compelling.

dimensions_used.Altitude: Optimize for product understanding and early-access interest; do not expand to product implementation.
dimensions_used.Depth: Require a useful interaction and rendered checks of the actual homepage, honest product status and CTA.
dimensions_used.Range: Borrow workshop feedback and editorial hierarchy as relationships; compare literal demonstration against gallery and temporal narrative.
dimensions_used.Speed: Reuse recovered brand assets, parallelize product demo and direction research, keep one meaningful interaction rather than a complex tour.

upgrades: Make the product demonstration carry the design
Explore composition and story, not color variations
Preserve factual and visual identity constraints
prompt_expansion.constraint_check: Pass: homepage only; existing identity retained; no Sites; no fictional capability, access, paid generation, publication permission, or testimonials inferred.

idea_inventory: Working canvas: owner requests a change inside a credible website workspace.
Business gallery: three full-size websites establish breadth before explaining tools.
Day after launch: new business needs become a simple sequence of site updates.
Before and after: compare an unclear offer with a clear business-specific page.
Private viewing: follow one customer action from homepage to enquiry.
One request: lead with a common owner request, then show the complete edited section.
A business owner's desk: project status and website preview replace files and email threads.
Editorial case note: one fictional business and a concrete communication problem.
Annotated document: make visual feedback resemble a familiar review process.
Launch checklist: show completed essentials as a compact practical opening.
Content first: headline, image, and action compose into a useful business story.
Customer journey: business need, site answer, next action in one continuous reading path.
Mobile first: a phone-sized business site establishes usefulness before desktop controls.
Desktop/mobile comparison: same site shows responsive outcomes with a simple toggle.
One surface, many businesses: alternate genuine business contexts in a shared product frame.
Website health: static operational essentials explain continuing care without fabricated analytics.
Open page and review rail: a readable site with a narrow owner-feedback panel.
Three verbs: create, improve, and manage use different visual density and pacing.
Opportunity notice: an upcoming service launch triggers the example update.
Archive of improvements: a concise visible history supports continuity and control.
Portrait of a business: contextual image and brand copy explain why generic templates fall short.
Guided tour: linear short demo with explicit Next/Back and stable preview.
Comparison and approval: reversible original/updated states are the focal event.
Quiet product manifesto: plain audience questions answered through working UI examples.

shortlist.name: The working Studio
shortlist.premise: Understand the product by trying one useful local change
shortlist.composition: Outcome-led typography above a dominant website canvas and review rail
shortlist.strength: Immediate product recognition and a concrete differentiator
shortlist.risk: Demo must remain legible; avoid overly dense dashboard chrome

shortlist.name: The business gallery
shortlist.premise: Recognize the value through finished business website examples
shortlist.composition: Centered promise followed by three differently sized photographic business-site panels
shortlist.strength: Tangible business range and attractive output
shortlist.risk: May read as an agency portfolio or template marketplace; evidence-heavy

shortlist.name: The day after launch
shortlist.premise: Website improves as the business changes
shortlist.composition: Asymmetric headline with change history rail beside one evolving site
shortlist.risk: Weak initial product/category recognition; better as a supporting section

lineage.extracted_relationship: A coherent visible connection between an owner's request and the website result
lineage.substantive_change: Keep request and result in the same product frame

lineage.extracted_relationship: Separate stages coordinate around one shared object
lineage.substantive_change: Request/review/approval retain the same website canvas rather than replacing it with unrelated cards
lineage.decision: reinterpreted; no ribbons or ornamental folding

lineage.substantive_change: Would introduce control complexity unrelated to business owner intent

lineage.decision: retained as candidate, rejected as main direction

metaphor_comparison.boundary: No AI model or live publishing is executed

metaphor_comparison.mapping: Studio workbench with tools and drafts
metaphor_comparison.boundary: Physical workbench decoration adds no product understanding

metaphor_comparison.mapping: Business change and website change stay in step
metaphor_comparison.boundary: Use shared timing/cause-and-effect only, not abstract motion

limitations: Owner-context-led design; no customer research or measured conversion result.
Sampling aids coverage, not aesthetic certification.
